Yogi Berra was a Hall of Fame catcher and one of the Yankees' most beloved figures, combining exceptional hitting with a career two eighty-five average, clutch postseason performance, and wise, often paradoxical off-field observations that made him a cultural icon. His nineteen World Series appearances and ten championships with the Yankees made him baseball's winningest player.

Berra played nineteen seasons with the Yankees as catcher and occasional outfielder, winning ten World Series titles—more than any other player in history. He hit three hundred fifty-eight career home runs despite being a catcher, a position traditionally dominated by pitching and defense. A fifteen-time All-Star, Berra was a three-time American League MVP in nineteen fifty-one, nineteen fifty-four, and nineteen fifty-five.

Known for wise, paradoxical sayings such as "It ain't over till it's over" and "Nobody goes to that restaurant anymore—it's too crowded," Berra became a cultural icon. He managed the Yankees to the nineteen sixty-four World Series and later served as a coach across multiple franchises, remaining a Yankees ambassador for decades. Berra caught two perfect games, including Don Larsen's in the nineteen fifty-six World Series, demonstrating his exceptional rapport with pitchers.

Mickey Mantle was his contemporary and the Yankees' other centerpiece star. Whitey Ford was the ace pitcher Berra caught and worked closely with. Mariano Rivera was a later-era Yankees pitching legend Berra would have known. Berra spent his entire career with the Yankees franchise, becoming inseparable from it.
